leadingNumbers.text: A sound one nets about ten grand and a bad one loses about nine. To compare the checks with the stakes, what does a typical machine cost you at the hammer: the lowest, the usual and the highest you have bought?

readiness: ok   Every element has a value or a range | Every part is filed.

ok   The tension names something that flips the best choice | A fleet seller with full service records and a price under about $45,000: he would bid without inspecting. Timing can also force it: with two days left he cannot book the inspector, so he has to pass or bid blind.
ok   Newcomer and professional are each written as a rule
ok   The outcome can be computed in money
open Every number has a range and a source | 36 numbers: 10 without a range, 7 without a source, 2 marked as a guess.
ok   Three worked situations, one of them where the obvious choice is wrong | 3 with a choice and a reason.
open No two answers disagree | 4 found by the audit, 0 worked situations where the stated rule and the stated choice differ.
ok   The expert has approved the read-back | Approved 2026-10-09.
missed: Financing: a slow machine costs more than the repair bill. About 9% a year is paid on the money tied up, so a bad machine sitting two or three months bleeds interest, and it uses up room under the $400,000 cap so he cannot buy something better. He says this never shows up on the repair list.
Correction from the expert: he earlier said the inspection catches pretty much everything, which was loose talk. It catches about seven in ten and misses the intermittent hydraulic faults.
